analysis.title: Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX.O): Adding Upside 90-Day Catalyst Watch
key_insights: Citi opens a positive 90-day Catalyst Watch (Upside) on SPCX, rated Buy with a US$240 target price versus a US$147.79 close on 20 Oct 2026, implying 62.4% expected total return.
Catalyst 1: SPCX has a track record of beats and raises, which Citi expects to continue into 4Q26.
Catalyst 2: Flight 15 is expected to be a major space-industry catalyst that sets the stage for rapid reusability at a scale not yet demonstrated in launch.
Catalyst 3: Citi sees evidence that $/watt is trending significantly above consensus expectations.
Catalyst 4: Grok model release cadence is expected to continue and accelerate.
Catalysts 5 and 6: Citi sees possible additional detail before year-end on SPCX's differentiated power-generation solutions and its evolving mobile strategy.
Citi describes SPCX as in the midst of a catalyst-rich 2-3 year arc and sees the next 2-3 months as especially catalyst rich.
Buy thesis rests on launch capabilities, scaling space infrastructure into Orbital AI and Starlink opportunities, extreme vertical integration, and differentiated margin and growth profiles.

The $240 base-case target averages three methods: 2027E growth-adjusted multiples for a basket of trillion-dollar comps, a sum-of-the-parts (Space, Connectivity, AI) on 2027E growth-adjusted multiples, and 2030E comparable-company multiples for the same basket.
Citi EPS estimates sit well above First Call consensus: 2027E $3.25 versus $1.83 and 2028E $8.07 versus $4.64, while 2026E is $0.46 versus consensus -$0.02.

trade_ideas.description: Long SPCX via a 90-day positive Catalyst Watch, Buy rating, $240 target
trade_ideas.rationale: Beats and raises, Flight 15 reusability, $/watt above consensus, Grok cadence and possible power-gen and mobile detail before year-end.
trade_ideas.risk: Failure to demonstrate rapid Starship reusability, lack of launch infrastructure, FAA and other regulatory headwinds, slow Starlink mobile share gains, failure to show AI orbital compute satellites.

risk_factors: Failure to demonstrate rapid reusability on Starship.
Regulatory headwinds from the FAA and other government organizations.
Failure to rapidly gain market share in Starlink mobile.
Failure to demonstrate AI orbital satellites capable of compute.
